HybridPilot
ML Ratchet · vehicle project · Phase 2Trained on physics. Graded on reality.

HybridPilot

A hybrid has to decide, every second, whether to burn fuel or spend battery. The offline optimum (dynamic programming) knows the whole trip in advance. HybridPilot is a 16,000-parameter network that learned the optimum's price of battery charge from 2,000 simulated trips and decides causally, from the past and present alone.

Engine on (bar) or off (gap), second by second, on a real 25-minute Ann Arbor route, Prius-like twin.

Inside the decision

The network, running in your browser

Each second the network reads 66 numbers and returns two: s, the fuel joules one joule of battery energy is worth right now, and P(on), its guess at whether DP would run the engine. The controller then picks the control that minimises P_fuel + s × P_battery, plus start fuel when starting, and adds SOC feedback to s. Start from a real moment of a recorded drive and change the state.

–s, network + SOC feedback
–s, network alone
–P(engine on)
Line: s across the battery window for this moment (network alone, dashed; with SOC feedback, solid). Higher s makes battery energy dearer, so the engine runs more and charges.

Ratchet

Every rung, kept or not

A rung is kept only if it closes more than 0.01 more of the rule strategies' fuel gap to DP on the frozen simulated set (106 trips, 18 vehicle classes, held-out vehicles and routes) and passes the dev gate: the 16 dev VED cars' routes, % of DP no worse than 0.2 points and charge-holding no worse than 3 points.

How it was built

Teacher, student, and an honest yardstick

  1. Vehicles and routes. 400 generated hybrids from RoadSim's generator: power-split, P2 parallel and series HEVs, power-split and series plug-ins, city buses, Class 6 and Class 8 trucks. Routes: 835 real Ann Arbor trips from VED's unlabelled train_noise cars (speed, lidar grade, airport weather), EPA and heavy-duty cycles with random weather, and synthetic city, suburban, highway, hilly and bus-stop routes. Warm fragments and cold soaks, −20 to 36 °C.
  2. Teacher. For each trip, DP solves the Bellman recursion over (engine on/off, SOC) on RoadSim's own candidate controls. Its cost-to-go table J(t, SOC) gives, at any state, the optimal action and the costate s* = −∂J/∂SOC ÷ (Voc·Q): the fuel value of one joule of battery energy. For HEVs a second pass values end-of-trip charge at the trip's typical s*, so labels near the end keep a causal meaning.
  3. Student. An MLP (66 → 96 → 96 → 2, tanh, 15,938 parameters) regresses log s* and classifies DP's on/off choice. Inputs: vehicle parameters (architecture, mass, engine and motor power per kg, battery kWh, CdA, Crr, SOC window), state (SOC, engine temperature and on/off timers, battery limits, cabin-heat flag), the past trace (EMAs of speed and power demand), optional preview bins up to 60 s, optional remaining distance. Preview length and nav were randomised during training so one network serves every setting.
  4. DAgger. Round 0: 800 trips driven by DP with random exploration bursts. Round 1: 600 trips driven by the round-0 network (teacher in control 30 % of seconds), every visited state labelled by DP. A second round did not help (rung R6).
  5. Policy search. A small evolution strategy tuned the decision knobs (s scale and bias, SOC-feedback gain, minimum on/off times, on/off-head weight) on 60 training-distribution trips. It traded a little fuel for less engine chatter and was rejected by the frozen set.
  6. Grading. For every strategy on every trip, DP is re-solved to end at that strategy's own final SOC, so fuel is compared at matched battery energy. "% of DP" = 1 − (fuel − DP fuel at matched energy) ÷ (DP fuel when sustaining the start SOC).
Limits

Where it fails, and what this cannot show

    Use it

    The release

    hybridpilot-v1.0.zip: a numpy module (features + network + decision rule), the weights, a RoadSim adapter, demo.py on three real VED exam trips (7 s), the model card and every training script. The network needs only numpy and scipy; the candidate controls come from a powertrain model, RoadSim's or your own.

    import hybridpilot as HP
# inside RoadSim
from roadsim import simulate
out = simulate(spec, trip, strategy=HP.make_roadsim_strategy(preview_s=0, nav=False))

# with your own powertrain model, each second:
core = HP.HybridPilotCore()
x = HP.features(vf, tc, vp, state, ctx, preview_s=30)        # 66 causal features
j, s, p_on = core.decide(x, soc, soc_ref, phev, P_fuel, P_chem, on, ok,
                         eng_on, t_on, t_off, start_W)       # index of the chosen control

    Data and credits

    Vehicle Energy Dataset (VED), G. S. Oh, D. J. LeBlanc, H. Peng, IEEE T-ITS 2020, Apache-2.0: Ann Arbor routes (speed, GPS) and logged fuel, rpm and SOC. USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar (public domain) for grade. Iowa Environmental Mesonet ASOS weather. ZTBus, F. Widmer et al., ETH Zurich, CC-BY-4.0 (Zurich bus routes). EPA dynamometer schedules and 40 CFR 1037 cycles (public domain). Simulator: RoadSim (ML Ratchet Phase 1): EPA ALPHA engine and motor maps, checked against EPA test results and NREL FASTSim. Real-data packaging: RoadData (Phase 1). DP after Sundström and Guzzella's dpm practice; ECMS after Paganelli et al. 2002, A-ECMS after Onori, Serrao and Rizzoni 2010; DAgger after Ross, Gordon and Bagnell 2011.
